skill.name: emailautomationskill
skill.description: Plan, audit, and improve email automation workflows with clear trigger contracts, QA checks, governance rules, and approval gates.
skill.summary: Guide email automation planning, QA, governance, and lifecycle journey reviews.
skill.author: Sequenzy

security_audit.summary: Static analysis reported no suspicious patterns across 3 scanned files. Manual context review found prompt-only guidance for email automation governance and approval gates. No semantic security findings were identified.

content.value_statement: Email automations can create duplicate sends, stale journeys, or consent mistakes. This skill helps agents review triggers, QA plans, and approval gates.
actual_capabilities: Drafts automation contracts with triggers, eligibility, waits, exits, and success events.
Builds trigger inventories for lifecycle, behavioral, transactional, and reactivation journeys.
Creates QA plans for branches, exits, suppression checks, event delays, and rollback steps.
Reviews overlapping automations for duplicate sends, conflicting offers, and frequency pressure.
Defines governance rules for ownership, approvals, change logs, and review cadence.
Recommends journey improvements while separating advice from live-system actions.
limitations: It does not send emails, import contacts, or edit live automations.
Recommendations depend on the journey details, metrics, and screenshots supplied by the user.
Provider-specific steps are described operationally, not as guaranteed platform commands.
It cannot verify consent, suppression state, or event reliability without source evidence.

use_cases.title: Audit a Lifecycle Journey
use_cases.description: Review a welcome, onboarding, or reactivation journey for missing exits, stale contacts, and unclear success metrics.

use_cases.title: Create an Automation QA Plan
use_cases.description: Turn branches, waits, suppressions, and test contacts into a practical pre-launch checklist.

use_cases.title: Govern Production Changes
use_cases.description: Define approval gates, ownership, rollback notes, and review cadence before a live automation is changed.

prompt_templates.title: Map a Journey Contract
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to write a journey contract for my email automation. Include trigger, eligibility, waits, exits, suppression checks, and success event.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Trigger Inventory
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to inventory my automation triggers. Group them by lifecycle stage, source event, owner, status, and production risk.

prompt_templates.title: Review Launch QA
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a launch QA plan. Cover test contacts, branches, exits, event delays, suppression rules, and rollback steps.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Overlapping Automations
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to audit overlapping journeys. Find duplicate sends, conflicting offers, frequency-cap pressure, stale enrollment, and approval gaps.

output_examples.input: Audit an abandoned-cart journey before launch.
output: Journey contract with trigger, eligibility, waits, exits, suppression checks, and success metric.
QA checklist covering test contacts, branch coverage, delayed events, and rollback ownership.
Approval gate for activation, suppression edits, and any production automation change.
Risk summary for stale contacts, missing exits, weak event freshness, and frequency pressure.
Recommended cleanup plan with owner, approval path, and recovery metric.
Evidence list showing which supplied fields or metrics support each recommendation.

output_examples.input: Plan governance for a lifecycle automation library.
output: Naming rules, owner fields, change log expectations, and scheduled review cadence.
Risk gates for drafts, segment recommendations, imports, suppression edits, and live changes.
Handoff notes that separate analysis from actions requiring approval.

best_practices: Provide trigger sources, event schema, suppression rules, and current journey status before asking for recommendations.
Ask for evidence notes so each recommendation links back to supplied data.
Use explicit approval gates before imports, live sends, suppression edits, or production journey changes.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to activate, deactivate, or edit a live journey without human approval.
Do not assume missing consent, suppression, or event fields are valid.
Do not optimize copy before confirming triggers, exits, branch coverage, and rollback planning.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps plan, audit, and improve email automations, lifecycle journeys, QA checks, and governance workflows.

faq.question: Can it send emails or change automations?
faq.answer: No. It separates recommendations from live-system actions and calls for explicit approval before risky changes.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide triggers, eligibility rules, waits, exits, suppression rules, screenshots, metrics, owners, and approval process details.

faq.question: Does it support provider-specific platforms?
faq.answer: It can describe provider-specific steps in operational language, but users must verify details inside their platform.

faq.question: How does it reduce automation risk?
faq.answer: It checks exits, suppressions, event delays, duplicate sends, frequency pressure, rollback steps, and ownership before launch.
